label: OK
gloss: no wording problem a careful editor would act on

label: VAGUE
gloss: refers in general where an exact file, command, column, count, or actor is available (doc-craft: Be concrete)

label: REFERENT
gloss: a pronoun, "this", or a definite phrase without one clear referent, or a term used before it is introduced (Qualified writing rule 1)

label: BARE
gloss: a noun phrase or quantifier that does not say which one, whose, or how many (Qualified writing rule 4)

label: TERM
gloss: shorthand, a coinage, slang, or a figurative name that a general reader would not know (Qualified writing rule 2)

label: REGISTER
gloss: informal, awkward, wordy, or ungrammatical phrasing that a plain, dry register would write differently

label: ABSOLUTE
gloss: never, always, every, or a claim stated more strongly than it can be checked (doc-craft: Hedge)

label: NARRATIVE
gloss: history, discovery steps, or authoring commentary in place of current behavior (doc-craft: State current reality)

label: SURPLUS
gloss: removable without changing what a reader does, or repeats another unit (doc-craft: Earn each sentence)

label: RESTRICTION
gloss: a non-obvious restriction missing its trigger, failure symptom, or mitigation (doc-craft: Format non-obvious restrictions)
